thread:
emma_support: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) escalated — users are getting kicked back to the login screen immediately after completing SSO + MFA. Happens only in Chrome. They say it's a 're-auth loop'. (came in via support ticket)
emma_support: Repro notes from customer:
1) Click 'Sign in with SSO' -> Okta flow -> completes MFA -> redirect back to /auth/callback
2) UI shows loading, then instant redirect to /login
3) Session never appears to stick; cookies show up in response but are not sent on subsequent request from browser

emma_support: Pasting the customer's network capture (sanitized):
```
POST /auth/callback 302 Found
Set-Cookie: RedwoodSession=eyJ...; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure
Location: https://app.acme.example/dashboard
```
Request when browser follows redirect to app.acme.example/dashboard: no Cookie header was sent.

alex_eng: :eyes: can you confirm whether the redirect crosses registrable domains? i.e. auth.redwood.example -> app.acme.example is cross-site. Chrome will block SameSite=Lax for POST->GET redirect flows sometimes.

samir_security: This looks like a SameSite issue on the session cookie. If the cookie is set with `SameSite=Lax` it will be sent on top-level GET navigations, but the OIDC flow involves a POST/302 exchange and then a cross-site GET. Chrome 109+ tightened some heuristics. Also confirm cookie has `Secure` and not missing `SameSite=None` for third-party cross-site flows.

customer_acme: Confirmed it's only happening when our IdP (okta.acme) redirects back. Safari/Firefox seem fine, chrome repros reproducibly.

olivia_sre-bot: We've seen similar reports — 2025-11 cookie rotation changed default samesite handling for a subset of routes; possible we missed the OIDC callback path. Tagging eng-runtime.

alex_eng: Steps I'll run locally to repro:
1) Start a local app with host header app.acme.local (hosts file mapping)
2) Use our staging IdP redirect to /auth/callback
3) Capture headers with `curl -v` and in Chrome devtools network

emma_support: customer provided curl that reproduces server-side behavior (cookies in response):
```
curl -i -L -X POST 'https://auth.redwood.example/auth/callback' \
  -H 'Host: app.acme.example' \
  --data 'code=XXX&state=YYY'
```
Response includes `Set-Cookie: RedwoodSession=...; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly; Secure` and a 302 -> app.acme.example/dashboard. Browser follow doesn't send the cookie.

maria_oncall: Quick mitigation suggestion: set `SameSite=None; Secure` on session cookies when the request includes an `iss` or `client_id` indicating third-party SSO redirect. We should be careful to only do this for OIDC callback flows to avoid CSRF exposure.

samir_security: Agreed but we need to audit CSRF token handling on that codepath. If we loosen SameSite we must ensure `state` validation and anti-forgery checks are enforced. Also log any changes for compliance trace.

alex_eng: I found code in `auth_service/session_manager.go` — default cookie attributes are set there. Looks like the cookie profile used during normal login sets SameSite=Lax, but the OIDC callback uses the same profile. Will propose computing cookie attrs dynamically based on `is_oidc_callback` boolean.

emma_support: Customer wants a fix ASAP — can we get a targeted hotfix for dedicated/private customers and a patch for hosted?

olivia_sre-bot: Suggestion: feature-flag rollout. For hosted: enable `samesite-oidc-fix` in prod region for a small percentage to measure. For dedicated: patch and ship a point release.

alex_eng: I'll open an internal PR and include:
- change cookie on OIDC callback to `SameSite=None; Secure; Domain=.redwood.example; Path=/; HttpOnly`
- keep audit log of state verification
- add E2E test that simulates cross-site redirect in headless Chrome

samir_security: Add a unit test verifying `state` match and that we reject if absent. Also a test to ensure cookie isn't `None` for normal non-SSO flows (defense in depth).

emma_support: For immediate workaround for the customer: ask them to try incognito and disable any extensions (they already tried incognito). Also ask them to test with Flag `chrome://flags/#treat-unknown-samesite-as-lax` (not ideal). Better: we can enable temporary redirect landing page on same registrable domain as auth that sets the cookie before redirecting to app.acme.example — i.e. top-level set-cookie step. Would you prefer we spin that up?

customer_acme: We can try the landing page if you can host it. We need the users back in <24h if possible.

maria_oncall: I'll coordinate a temporary proxy landing route `https://link.redwood.example/oidc-landing?next=https://app.acme.example/dashboard` that will set the session cookie on link.redwood.example (same site as auth) before redirecting. Not ideal long term but faster.

alex_eng: Notes for PR: code patch + release notes must mention that SSO cookie attr changed for OIDC flows. Add a migration note for customers using strict cookie policies.

samir_security: Also check behavior for cross-subdomain flows (auth.redwood.example -> app.redwood.example) — we might only need `Domain=.redwood.example` and keep SameSite=Lax in that case. Distinguish cross-registrable-domain vs cross-subdomain.

emma_support: Action items:
- alex_eng: open PR, include tests, target hotfix (ETA 6 hours)
- maria_oncall: stand up temporary landing proxy and coordinate with customer (ETA 2 hours)
- samir_security: audit state/csrf checks + add tests (ETA 4 hours)
- olivia_sre-bot: enable rollout flag once PR passes

customer_acme: Thanks — let us know when the proxy is reachable. We'll test and report.

olivia_sre-bot: Incident tag created: #INC-2026-1202-mfa-sso-cookie. Assigning to alex_eng.

alex_eng: I'll post the PR link here when ready and kick off the canary. Will also include a quick repro script for Chrome headless so support can verify with the customer. :thumbsup:

emma_support: Closing loop for now. I'll update the ticket with the landing proxy URL when Maria confirms. :white_check_mark:
